executive_summary.question: What punishment applies to abetment of an offence when the Sanhita makes no express provision for punishing that specific abetment?
executive_summary.generated_answer:
When the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) contains **no express provision** for punishing a particular act of abetment, the punishment is determined by the following rules (as set out in the Sanhita): | Situation | Punishment (when no express provision for abetment) | Source | |-----------|------------------------------------------------------|--------| | **The act abetted is actually committed** (i.e., the offence occurs because of the abetment) | The abettor receives **the same punishment as the principal offender** for that offence. | [e3cfd376-1174-46eb-9573-2b6cafe0dbc6] – § 49 | | **The offence is punishable with death or imprisonment for life** and the offence **is not committed** as a result of the abetment | Imprisonment of either description for a term **up to seven years**, **plus fine**.
If, in consequence of the abetment, any hurt is caused to a person, the term may extend to **fourteen years**, **plus fine**. | [320c1526-fed5-4985-ae85-e16910f24ab6] – § 55 (and its illustration) | | **The offence is punishable with imprisonment** (but not death or life) and the offence **is not committed** as a result of the abetment | Imprisonment of any description provided for that offence for a term **up to one‑fourth of the longest term** prescribed for the offence, **or fine, or both**.
If the abettor (or the person abetted) is a public servant whose duty is to prevent such offence, the term may extend to **one‑half of the longest term** (or fine, or both). | [a90a5461-96e5-4ff3-b754-c6e6c504fe4e] – § 56 | | **If the act abetted is done with a different intention or knowledge** (but still constitutes the offence) | The abettor is punished **as if the act had been done with the abettor’s intention or knowledge** (i.e., the punishment for the offence that would have resulted). | [e3cfd376-1174-46eb-9573-2b6cafe0dbc6] – § 50 | | **If a different act is done** (but is a probable consequence of the abetment) | The abettor is liable for the act actually done, **in the same manner and to the same extent** as if he had directly abetted that act. | [e3cfd376-1174-46eb-9573-2b6cafe0dbc6] – § 51 | **In short:** - When the abetted offence **occurs**, the abettor gets the **same punishment** as the offender. - When it **does not occur**, the punishment scales with the seriousness of the offence: up to 7 years (or 14 years if hurt results) for death/life‑imprisonment offences; up to one‑fourth (or one‑half for public servants) of the maximum imprisonment term for other imprisonable offences, plus any applicable fine. These rules are drawn directly from sections 49, 50, 51, 55, and 56 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 as shown in the cited context chunks.
